chapter_title: Chương 251: 0253【Tranh cãi truyền thông từ 26 giây】

segments.title: Chương 251: 0253【Tranh cãi truyền thông từ 26 giây】
segments.content:
The number of students in the cafeteria grew larger and larger.

Some were there to eat, others to watch TV. Having heard that the event organized by Chen Guiliang was going to be on the *Xinwen Lianbo* news broadcast, they all sat and waited, wanting to know what kind of event it was.

No one guessed it was the Sanguosha National Collegiate League!

Five minutes passed, ten minutes passed, twenty minutes passed, twenty-five minutes passed... and still, there was no news related to Chen Guiliang.

"Old Chen, did CCTV stand you up?" one student said.

Another student said, "Yeah, President Chen, I hear CCTV often changes their content at the last minute."

Chen Guiliang shouted, "Quiet down, everyone's getting a share. After we finish watching *Xinwen Lianbo*, it's my treat. We'll go indulge ourselves outside the south gate, barbecue, malatang, whatever you want. As long as you don't eat till you burst, you can eat your fill!"

"President Chen is the man!" someone immediately cheered.

Someone else made a joke from a Hong Kong/Taiwan drama: "Everyone's got a share, Young Master Chen is covering the bill tonight."

There were also cries of sorrow: "Damn it, I just ate dinner. I'm already stuffed, why didn't you say you were treating us sooner?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Those who've eaten, go pick out two drinks."

"I want a bottle of Nutrition Express!"

"I want a Red Bull."

"Hey, you're all picking the expensive stuff. I want a bottle of '82 Lafite!"

A bunch of lunatics who didn't go home for summer break.

Just as the news was about to end, the female anchor faced the camera and said, "Next, here is a news brief..."

"Today, the entire army and the WJ forces held a series of activities to celebrate the 79th anniversary of the army's founding..."

"The main structure of the Beijing Olympics Main Press Center has been capped, and the Water Cube has completed the installation of its membrane structure. The Olympic Organizing Committee has stated that all competition venues will be completed by the end of the year..."

"The 'Peace Mission 2006' joint China-Russia military exercise has entered its second phase. Today, a land-air coordinated combat drill was conducted in XX, Lu Province..."

One news brief after another aired, and soon there were less than 30 seconds left.

Finally, the female anchor said, "The second Sanguosha National Collegiate League concluded yesterday at the Shanghai New International Expo Center. A total of 16 teams participated in the offline competition, including six university representative teams from Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, who either competed or were invited to watch. This is the first time that universities from China's three regions have competed on the same stage due to a domestic game..."

Even on the *Xinwen Lianbo* news broadcast, it was referred to as "three regions across the strait" at the time.

A news brief is usually around 20 seconds, with some longer ones reaching 30 seconds.

Chen Guiliang stared at the time at the bottom of the TV screen and calculated that the news brief for the Sanguosha National League was 26 seconds long.

For a news brief, that was quite a respectable length.

The news footage mainly showed leaders shaking hands with the players, enthusiastic exchanges between players from both sides of the strait, cosplay performances, as well as shots of the competition and the audience. The camera scanned across the front row, and Chen Guiliang, Tao Chenggang, and others appeared on screen for about two or three seconds.

"Ah! Ah! Ah!"

In her rented room, Xu Fengyin cheered under her breath and took out her phone to call her family, wanting to tell her parents she had been on *Xinwen Lianbo*.

But after opening her contact list, she didn't dial.

She had appeared on screen because she was cosplaying Zhen Ji on stage, which was slightly suggestive of showing cleavage, and the camera had even lingered on her for a second.

How was she supposed to explain this to her parents?

Forget it.

Her parents were old-fashioned.

Xu Fengyin was currently renting an old and rundown small apartment in Zhongguan West District. The owner was a former big shot from the Chinese Academy of Sciences, but he had long since moved his entire family to a better house. This shabby cylinder-shaped building was built in the 70s, and you even had to go outside to find a public toilet.

The main reason was that it was close to the company, otherwise who would rent here?

Xu Fengyin had lived here for over half a year and had decided to move. It didn't matter if it was more expensive or farther away.

She was now a senior artist at Game Science, and her monthly salary had already risen to 7,500 yuan. In the industry, this was considered upper-middle level, but Xu Fengyin's performance bonuses were especially high.

Because the character portraits and hero skins she drew sold well!

Her savings from a year and a half were already enough for a down payment on a mid-range small apartment in Beijing.

"Sigh, should I rent or buy?" Xu Fengyin lay on the peeling old sofa, inexplicably troubled.

She wasn't sharing the apartment with anyone; she had always lived alone.

Mainly because she often drew risqué comics and was afraid of being seen by a roommate.

The room was always a mess, with drafts, tools, and daily necessities strewn everywhere. If an outsider saw it, they would think the house had been robbed.

"So boring!"

Most of the time, Xu Fengyin enjoyed living alone, but occasionally she would feel bored and wish there was someone by her side.

Might as well read some manga.

As an old pro, Xu Fengyin had a collection of many forums, like Man You Forum, Tian Xiang Xiao Zhu, and so on. In the hidden sections, by paying points, you could download compressed files of a certain kind of manga.

If you hung around those places long enough and got to know some elusive masters, you could even mail-order authentic but not-so-proper manga from Japan.

Her dark history being exposed?

That minor account that was dug up was nothing. The veteran pro Xu still had plenty of alternate accounts.

Hugging a manga book, Xu Fengyin soon became engrossed in reading. It seemed there were bugs in this rundown house, and she squirmed around on the sofa.

As expected, without Chen Guiliang having to take the initiative to promote it, the reaction from the print media was very fast.

But some very interesting scenes also emerged.

The editor-in-chief on duty at *Guangming Daily* frowned and called the reporter who wrote the article: "What on earth is Sanguosha? From your article, it seems to be an online game. This thing actually made it onto *Xinwen Lianbo*?"

The reporter explained, "Sanguosha was originally a tabletop game, a card game played on a table. It's different from poker; it has its own characters and rules. Since mahjong and poker can be moved online, so can tabletop games. So now, Sanguosha is also considered an online game."

The editor-in-chief suddenly understood, "Is it like bridge? Yes, bridge played online."

"Well... it's not quite like that," the reporter racked his brains, not knowing how to describe it, and could only explain in detail, "In Sanguosha, there are general cards based on historical figures from the Three Kingdoms period, like Cao Cao, Liu Bei, and Sun Quan. These generals have skills. Liu Bei's two skills are called 'Benevolence' and 'Rally.' 'Benevolence' is giving two cards to others. 'Rally' is having generals from allied states help you attack enemies."

"Oh, I understand," the editor-in-chief praised. "This game is indeed different. It contains historical and cultural elements, and it also attracted students from Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan. No wonder it could be on *Xinwen Lianbo*. Alright, no problem, I'm hanging up."

In fact, that reporter was also just repeating what he had learned.

Of course, the reporter knew of Chen Guiliang and had heard of Sanguosha, but he had never played it.

When he was writing the article, he specifically searched the Sanguosha official website, where there were detailed introductions to the gameplay and cards.

After some research, the reporter finally understood what Sanguosha was all about.

The last time Chen Guiliang had angrily criticized *Wolf Totem*, although *Guangming Daily* had initially spoken up for *Wolf Totem*, it immediately shut up when it saw the tide turning.

In the past year, *Guangming Daily* had been relentlessly attacked by Fang Zhouzi, and Fang Zhouzi's platform for his attacks was the *China Youth Daily*.

It all started when *Guangming Daily* reported on a major domestic scientific and technological achievement. This achievement was not fabricated, but its role and status were overly exaggerated. An extremely ordinary achievement was hyped up by *Guangming Daily* as a world-class breakthrough.

Fang Zhouzi and Academician He both entered the fray to debunk it.

These two debunkers were also quite comical. They joined forces to expose this academic fraud, but the articles they wrote contradicted each other. If Fang's article was valid, then He's article was basically nonsense. They never seemed to realize this problem.

To put it bluntly, it was two academic half-wits joining forces to criticize a bragging researcher from the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

*Guangming Daily*'s stance was to hype, hype, hype. First, it hyped up *Wolf Totem*, then it hyped up that researcher, and now it was hyping up Chen Guiliang's Sanguosha.

This time, *Guangming Daily* hyped Sanguosha as the pride of national games.

The news of Sanguosha going international had already been glorified on the Sanguosha official website. When the *Guangming Daily* reporter saw the news on the website, he once again used his imagination to embellish it.

In this reporter's writing, Sanguosha, with its elements of Chinese history and culture, had not only become a sensation in Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, but had also caused a stir in Japan and South Korea. Players in Japan and South Korea were learning Chinese history through the game, appreciating the profoundness of Chinese culture.

The game's distributor in Singapore not only introduced Sanguosha there but also promoted it throughout Southeast Asia.

The reporter even fabricated an online interview with a Singaporean netizen: "I particularly like Sanguosha. After playing this game, I specifically bought and read *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*. I hope to study in China in the future..."

Do reporters from official media not fabricate things?

Even reporters from X*n*ua News Agency would fabricate interview content!

Besides *Guangming Daily* helping to hype it up, the *Strait Herald* naturally also gave its full support, but tried to downplay the online game element. Its article title was: "Sanguosha Tabletop Game Becomes a Cultural Bridge, Bringing Students from Both Sides of the Strait and Three Regions Together."

And *The Beijing News*, which had sided with Chen Guiliang last time, began to sing a different tune this time.

It seemed that *Guangming Daily* and *The Beijing News* were both repeatedly flip-flopping.

But that was not the case; they had their own firm positions.
